title: The Gazette
tagline: What mattered this week — curated, condensed, and set in type.

articles.headline: Harbor lights return as the night ferry resumes weekend runs
articles.dek: After pier repairs, the Saturday crossing is back

blocks.alt: Night ferry approaching the lit pier
blocks.caption: The Saturday night run slips back into the harbor.

blocks.text: The night ferry slipped back into the harbor on Saturday under a sky thick with salt and sodium light. For the first time since July, the pier gates stayed open past dusk, and the usual crowd filled the waiting shed as if the summer never left.
Dockworkers finished the last of the piling wraps on Thursday. Engineers signed off Friday morning. Weekend runs resume on the usual half-hour cadence through midnight.
Tickets remain the same price. Bikes board first on the lower deck; the upper cabin stays walk-up only until the holiday schedule posts.
If a dense fog advisory is in effect, the ferry may run on visual approach and add five to ten minutes.

blocks.alt: Open water under a soft sky
blocks.caption: Remote image example (newsletter CDN / HTTPS URL).

blocks.text: Harbor staff said the first weekend back already felt like midsummer: musicians on the pier, coffee carts past ten, and the long horn sounding again across the channel.

articles.headline: Central Library opens the glass reading wing
articles.dek: Skylights, quiet rooms, plane trees

blocks.text: The new east wing of Central Library opened Monday after ten years of capital campaigns. Visitors walk into a double-height reading hall lit by north-facing glass and pale oak baffles.
Skylights run the length of the wing. Quiet rooms book in two-hour slots; plane trees shade the south terrace.
All stacks and study carrels remain free. Timed tickets are only for the rare-book gallery.

articles.headline: Neighborhood substations finish the quiet grid upgrade
articles.dek: Overnight work ends; heat-wave risk drops
articles.body: The last of twelve neighborhood substations completed a multi-year hardening project on Wednesday, swapping aging transformers for units rated for longer heat waves and sharper evening peaks. Utility crews worked mostly between midnight and dawn.

articles.headline: Farmers’ market extends into November
articles.dek: Late squash, cellar apples, pressed cider
articles.body: The Saturday market on Civic Plaza will run three extra weeks this year, organizers announced, citing milder forecasts and strong September attendance. Live music moves indoors to the arcade if rain arrives.

articles.headline: Voters clear a school bond for science labs
articles.dek: Narrow margin; work after spring term
articles.body: A $48 million school facilities bond passed by just under two points Tuesday night, funding science lab renovations at three middle schools and covered bus shelters at every elementary campus.

articles.headline: Community choir books the old Lyric Theater
articles.dek: Two December evenings; youth ushers benefit
articles.body: The Harbor Community Choir will perform two December evenings at the restored Lyric Theater, its first local appearance since the marquee relit last spring. Tickets go on sale Friday.

articles.headline: Crews begin the decade’s bridge paint cycle
articles.dek: Lane shifts overnight through March
articles.body: Scaffolding went up on the west approach Monday as painters start a ten-year maintenance cycle. Night lane closures begin next week; daytime traffic remains two ways with a temporary zipper merge.

articles.headline: Walk-in clinic adds Sunday morning hours
articles.dek: Pilot through the holidays
articles.body: The Eastside walk-in clinic will open Sundays from eight to noon through early January, a pilot aimed at parents who miss weekday slots. Flu shots and basic labs are included; specialists still require weekday referral.

articles.headline: Commuter rail trims weekend delays after switch work
articles.dek: On-time rate climbs above ninety percent
articles.body: Weekend on-time performance on the coastal line rose above ninety percent after crews replaced a stubborn interlocking near Mile 14. Officials caution holiday crowds may still bunch trains after noon.

articles.headline: Anonymous gift funds free first Sundays at the museum
articles.dek: Three years covered; memberships unchanged
articles.body: The city museum will waive general admission every first Sunday for the next three years after an anonymous gift covered the projected shortfall. Special exhibitions may still carry a surcharge.

articles.headline: Volunteers pull a ton of trash from the river bend
articles.dek: Annual sweep draws a record turnout
articles.body: More than four hundred volunteers lined the south bend Saturday, filling dumpsters with bottles, tires, and shopping carts. Organizers said it was the largest turnout since the sweep began in 2011.

articles.headline: Corner bakery reopens with the original ovens
articles.dek: Sourdough at dawn; lines by seven
articles.body: After a fire last winter, the corner bakery on Oak lit its rebuilt deck ovens Monday. The first loaves sold out before eight; afternoon pastry slots now require a paper ticket from the counter.

articles.headline: Council softens height caps near the station
articles.dek: Six stories allowed on two corridors
articles.body: The council voted 5–2 to allow six-story residential buildings within two blocks of the central station, reversing a 2018 cap. Neighbors won deeper setbacks and a shadow study for winter sun.

articles.headline: Park path lights switch to warmer LEDs
articles.dek: Fewer glare complaints; same brightness
articles.body: Recreation staff finished swapping path fixtures for warmer LEDs along the lake loop. Astronomers and night walkers both lobbied for the change; motion sensors dim stretches after midnight.

articles.headline: Local logistics startup adds a night warehouse shift
articles.dek: Eighty roles; transit stipends included
articles.body: A Harbor Point logistics firm posted eighty night-shift roles with transit stipends after winning a regional grocery contract. Training starts in two cohorts; bilingual supervisors are prioritized.

articles.headline: High school senior wins the regional poetry prize
articles.dek: Reading set for the Lyric lobby
articles.body: A Harbor High senior took the regional poetry prize with a sequence about ferry foghorns. A free reading is scheduled in the Lyric lobby next Thursday; chapbooks print in a run of two hundred.

articles.headline: City clears blocked storm drains before the next front
articles.dek: Leaf crews work the lower wards
articles.body: Public works crews cleared leaf mats from storm drains across the lower wards ahead of a wet weekend. Residents can still report standing water through the city’s text tip line.

articles.headline: New daycare opens twenty sliding-scale spots
articles.dek: Lottery draws Friday at noon
articles.body: A nonprofit daycare near the college hill will open twenty sliding-scale infant and toddler spots next month. Families enter a Friday noon lottery; income verification follows for winners.

articles.headline: College radio returns to the air after antenna repair
articles.dek: Student DJs reclaim the midnight slot
articles.body: Campus radio signed back on at 91.7 after a month of antenna work. The midnight experimental slot returns this weekend; streaming stayed up throughout the outage.

articles.headline: Missing trail link finally stitches the waterfront path
articles.dek: Ribbon cutting Saturday at ten
articles.body: A half-mile missing link in the waterfront trail opens Saturday, connecting the ferry plaza to the bird sanctuary without a street detour. Bikes share the path; a painted slow zone marks the sanctuary edge.

articles.headline: Free tax clinic expands to evenings in November
articles.dek: Appointments open Monday
articles.body: The volunteer tax clinic will add Tuesday and Thursday evenings in November for seasonal workers. Appointments open Monday; bring last year’s return and a photo ID.

articles.headline: Fog advisory returns with the early cold snap
articles.dek: Ferries on visual approach till noon
articles.body: A dense fog advisory is in effect through midmorning as the first cold snap settles over the harbor. Ferries will run on visual approach; drivers are asked to use low beams on the bridge.

articles.headline: Alley mural wall gets a fresh coat and new map
articles.dek: Walking tour QR codes installed
articles.body: Artists finished a refreshed alley mural wall behind Market Street, adding a small map of past commissions and QR codes for a self-guided walking tour. The city funded primer and scaffolding only.

articles.headline: Glass bus shelter pilots heat for winter waits
articles.dek: Three stops in the north wards
articles.body: Transit authority installed heated glass shelters at three north-ward stops as a winter pilot. Sensors shut heat off when the shelter is empty; results will decide a wider rollout.

articles.headline: Orchard fair brings cider presses to the fairgrounds
articles.dek: Saturday only; dogs welcome on leash
articles.body: Growers haul presses and late pears to the fairgrounds Saturday for the annual orchard fair. Admission is a canned good for the food bank; leashed dogs are welcome outside the tasting tent.
